concepts.def: Single bespoke item; high cost per unit; e.g., custom furniture.
Set quantity made together; flexible; e.g., loaves of bread, school uniforms.
Continuous high volume on assembly line; e.g., cars, smartphones.
24/7 operation for very high volume; e.g., chemicals, paper.
Toyota's stock-control method delivering parts as needed to reduce storage.
Inspection at points of manufacture to ensure standards are met.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Manufacturing Processes & Techniques — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Manufacturing Processes & Techniques brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Manufacturing Processes & Techniques.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A bespoke wedding ring is which type?

numericals.q: How many main scales of production are commonly distinguished (one-off, batch, mass, continuous)?
